name: Port de Dunkerque
description: France's third-largest port, on the Flemish coast near the Belgian border. The marina sits inside the old commercial basin, a short walk from the town's WWII evacuation memorials.

name: Port de Boulogne-sur-Mer
description: France's leading fishing port, at the narrowest point of the Channel opposite Dover. The old walled town (Ville Haute) overlooks the harbour from its ramparts.

name: Port de Dieppe
description: One of France's oldest seaside resorts, with a marina right in the town centre below the 15th-century château overlooking the pebble beach.

name: Port de Plaisance du Havre
description: A major Channel container port at the mouth of the Seine, rebuilt by Auguste Perret after WWII — its concrete city centre is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Vieux Bassin de Honfleur
description: A picture-postcard Norman harbour of tall slate-fronted houses at the Seine estuary, long favoured by painters including Monet and the Impressionists.

name: Port de Deauville-Port-Morny
description: The genteel Norman resort of the famous boardwalk and its beach huts, twinned across the Touques river with Trouville-sur-Mer.

name: Port Chantereyne
description: A deep-water port on the tip of the Cotentin peninsula, sheltered by one of the world's largest artificial harbours — a natural staging point for Channel and Atlantic passages.

name: Port de Plaisance de Granville
description: A granite-walled corsair town on a rocky headland facing the Channel Islands, with some of Europe's largest tidal ranges.

name: Port Vauban
description: The walled corsair city of Brittany's north coast, its ramparts enclosing a dense old town just steps from the marina lock gates.

name: Port de Roscoff
description: A small granite ferry and fishing port on Brittany's north coast, historic gateway for the cross-Channel onion trade and today's link to Plymouth and Cork.

name: Port du Moulin Blanc
description: One of Europe's finest natural harbours (the Rade de Brest), and France's main naval base on the Atlantic — home port of the Tour de France à la Voile and biennial Brest maritime festival.

name: Port de Camaret-sur-Mer
description: A former sardine-fishing port at the foot of the Crozon peninsula, its harbour wall lined with the wrecks of old wooden boats left to decay in the tideline.

name: Port de Rosmeur
description: A historic sardine port on a wide bay in Finistère, now home to the Port-Musée and a fleet of restored traditional boats.

name: Port de Bénodet
description: A popular family resort at the mouth of the Odet river, a scenic tidal approach often called one of Brittany's prettiest river passages.

name: Port de Concarneau
description: Home to France's leading tuna fleet, wrapped around the fortified Ville Close islet in the middle of the harbour.

name: Port de Lorient (Kernevel)
description: A deep natural harbour built around a former WWII U-boat base, today one of the world's leading centres for offshore ocean-racing yacht design.

name: Port de La Trinité-sur-Mer
description: A leading French offshore-racing and multihull hub at the mouth of the Crac'h river, near the Carnac megaliths.

name: Port de Vannes
description: A walled Breton city at the head of the Gulf of Morbihan, its marina reached by a tidal channel winding past dozens of small islands.

name: Port de Pornic
description: A former fishing village on the south Brittany/Pays de la Loire border, its harbour overlooked by a 13th-century château once owned by Gilles de Rais.

name: Port-Joinville
description: The only town on the Île d'Yeu, a granite Atlantic island reachable only by boat, ringed by wild cliffs to the south and sandy coves to the north.

name: Port Olona
description: Start and finish port of the Vendée Globe round-the-world race, with a long sandy beach promenade lined by the old fishing quarter of La Chaume.

name: Port de Saint-Martin-de-Ré
description: A Vauban-fortified citadel port on the low, whitewashed island off La Rochelle, linked to the mainland by a 3 km toll bridge.

name: Port des Minimes
description: Europe's largest marina, just south of La Rochelle's medieval towered harbour entrance (Tour Saint-Nicolas / Tour de la Chaîne).

name: Port de Royan
description: A resort town at the mouth of the Gironde estuary, largely rebuilt in 1950s modernist style after wartime destruction, facing the Côte de Beauté.

name: Port d'Arcachon
description: Gateway to the Arcachon basin's oyster beds and the nearby Dune du Pilat, Europe's tallest sand dune.

name: Port de Bayonne / Anglet
description: A Basque country port at the confluence of the Adour and Nive rivers, close to the surf beaches of Anglet and Biarritz.

name: Port de Hendaye
description: France's southwesternmost coastal town, facing Spanish Hondarribia across the Bidasoa estuary at the foot of the Pyrenees.

name: Port Camargue
description: Europe's largest private marina, purpose-built in the 1970s with waterside villas lining every quay, next to the Camargue wetlands.

name: Port de Palavas-les-Flots
description: A lively Languedoc resort at the mouth of the Lez river, just south of Montpellier, popular for its beaches and seafood quays.

name: Port de Plaisance de Sète
description: A Mediterranean fishing port built on a rocky island (Mont Saint-Clair), crossed by canals and famous for its water-jousting tournaments.

name: Port du Cap d'Agde
description: One of the Mediterranean's largest marinas, built on volcanic black-stone shores near the ancient Greek-founded town of Agde.

name: Port de Gruissan
description: A circular village port built around its old salt-tower, between the Gruissan salt pans and the Mediterranean beaches.

name: Port de Port-Vendres
description: A deep natural harbour in French Catalonia near the Spanish border, sheltered below the vineyards of the Côte Vermeille.

name: Port de Toulon
description: Home port of the French Navy's Mediterranean fleet, in a deep bay ringed by Mont Faron, with a lively old-town market by the marina.

name: Port de Bandol
description: A Provençal resort known for its rosé vineyards and palm-lined seafront, a short sail from the Îles des Embiez.

name: Port de La Ciotat
description: Birthplace of cinema (the Lumière brothers' first screening) and of the pétanque game, with a historic shipyard now specialising in superyacht refits.

name: Port de Cassis
description: A pastel-hued fishing village tucked below limestone cliffs, the usual departure point for exploring the Calanques between Marseille and Cassis.

name: Vieux-Port de Marseille
description: The historic heart of France's oldest city, a working harbour since Greek antiquity, overlooked by the basilica of Notre-Dame-de-la-Garde.

name: Port du Frioul
description: A sheltered marina on the arid Frioul archipelago just offshore from Marseille, beside the island fortress of If (of Dumas' Count of Monte Cristo).

name: Port de Porquerolles
description: The main village port of the largest of the Îles d'Hyères, a car-free island of pine forest, vineyards and turquoise coves within a national park.

name: Port de Saint-Tropez
description: The legendary Riviera fishing-village-turned-jet-set harbour, its quayside cafés facing a wall of superyachts along the Môle Jean Réveille.

name: Vieux-Port de Cannes
description: The Croisette's home harbour beneath the Film Festival's Palais, with the medieval Suquet hill and its watchtower rising just behind the quay.

name: Port Vauban
description: Europe's largest yacht harbour, its 'Quai des Milliardaires' berthing some of the world's biggest private yachts beneath Vauban's 17th-century ramparts.

name: Port Lympia
description: A pastel 18th-century harbour tucked below Nice's Castle Hill, at the eastern end of the Promenade des Anglais and the Baie des Anges.

name: Port de Menton
description: France's last Riviera town before the Italian border, known for its lemon groves, belle-époque gardens and Jean Cocteau museum by the old port.

name: Vieux-Port de Bastia
description: Corsica's main commercial gateway on the Tyrrhenian coast, its Genoese-era old port ringed by tall ochre townhouses below the citadel.

name: Port de l'Île-Rousse
description: A Balagne coast resort founded by Pascal Paoli, its red-granite offshore islets giving the town its name.

name: Port de Calvi
description: A Genoese citadel town on a sweeping bay of the Balagne, backed by the granite peaks of Corsica's interior and a long pine-lined beach.

name: Port Tino Rossi
description: Napoleon Bonaparte's birthplace and Corsica's capital, its marina facing the citadel across a wide gulf toward the Îles Sanguinaires.

name: Port de Propriano
description: A sheltered harbour on the Gulf of Valinco in southern Corsica, gateway to the granite villages and prehistoric sites of the Alta Rocca.

name: Port de Bonifacio
description: A dramatic fjord-like inlet below a citadel perched on chalk-white limestone cliffs, at Corsica's southern tip facing Sardinia.

name: Port de Porto-Vecchio
description: A former Genoese salt-trading citadel on a deep gulf in southeast Corsica, close to the white sand beaches of Palombaggia and Santa Giulia.
